entry: Psychological trait marked by apprehension and inhibition in new social settings or when others may judge. Shyness, also called diffidence, is frequently associated with social avoidance and is considered a normal personality variant. It is distinct from social anxiety disorder, which impairs daily functioning. Although shyness can be an attribute of people with [[Self-esteem|low self-esteem]], it is often defined by concern about the negative evaluation of others, such as mocking or rejection. Genetic data suggest that shyness is heritable, though environmental factors such as child abuse or ridicule contribute to its development. Research indicates a positive correlation between childhood fearfulness and shyness, and higher cortisol levels in shy children are associated with increased susceptibility to illness. Shyness is distinct from introversion, which involves a preference for low-stimulation environments rather than fear of social judgment.

Breed of [[Cat|domestic cat]], one of the first distinctly recognized breeds. It was selectively bred from the Wichianmat landrace of [[Thailand]], known as Siam before 1939, beginning at the end of the 19th century. Siamese cats have a colorpoint coat resulting from a temperature-sensitive type of albinism, along with blue almond-shaped eyes, a wedge-shaped head and large wide-set ears. The breed was among the most popular in Europe and North America in the 19th century. Manuscripts describing the Wichianmat, the Tamra Maew, are thought to originate from the [[Ayutthaya Kingdom]]. In 1878, [[Rutherford B. Hayes|President Rutherford B. Hayes]] received the first documented Siamese to reach the United States. From the 1980s, traditional rounder "old-style" cats were re-established as a separate Thai breed. The Siamese also served as foundation stock for the Himalayan, the Balinese and other breeds.

Freshwater fish, *Betta splendens*, native to mainland [[Southeast Asia]]. It is one of more than 70 species in the genus *Betta* but the only one commonly called "betta," owing to its global popularity as a pet. Domesticated in the central plain of [[Thailand]] more than 1,000 years ago, it was first bred for [[Aggression|aggression]] and used in gambling matches akin to cockfighting. Its long history of [[Selective breeding|selective breeding]] has produced a wide variety of coloration and finnage. Males are highly territorial, and when kept together without a means of escape, fights usually kill one or both fish. A labyrinth organ allows the fish to tolerate low oxygen and take in surface air. The species is the national aquatic animal of Thailand, the primary breeder and exporter for the global aquarium market. In the wild it is listed as "vulnerable" by the IUCN because of pollution and habitat destruction.

Geographical region comprising all of North Asia, part of [[Russia]] since its conquest began in 1582. It extends from the [[Ural Mountains]] in the west to the [[Pacific Ocean]] in the east and covers over 13.1 million square kilometers (5,100,000 sq mi), about three-quarters of Russia's total area. Home to roughly a quarter of the country's population, Siberia is sparsely populated; Novosibirsk, Krasnoyarsk and Omsk are its largest cities. Winters are long and harsh, with a January average of −25 °C (−13 °F). Over 85% of the population is of European descent, chiefly Russian, although sizable Asian-lineage minorities include Turkic communities such as the Yakuts and Tuvans. The conquest concluded with the annexation of Chukotka in 1778.

Large region of volcanic rock in [[Siberia]], Russia. Basaltic lava covered a large expanse of Siberia in one of the largest volcanic events of the last 500 million years. Its eruptions continued for roughly two million years and spanned the Permian–Triassic boundary, which occurred around 251.9 million years ago. The traps are believed to be the primary cause of the [[Permian–Triassic extinction event]], the most severe in the geologic record. Today the area is covered by about 7 million km² (3 million sq mi) of basaltic rock, with a volume of around 4 million km³ (1 million cu mi).

Population of the tiger subspecies *Panthera tigris tigris*, native to [[China|northeast China]] and the Russian Far East. Called the Amur tiger, it was eradicated from the Korean Peninsula during Japanese rule between 1910 and 1945. It now lives mainly in the Sikhote-Alin mountain region of Primorsky Krai. Intensive conservation efforts kept the population stable for more than a decade, though surveys after 2005 indicated decline. An initial census in 2015 indicated 480–540 individuals, and about 756, including 200 cubs, were estimated in 2022. The Siberian tiger is genetically close to the now-extinct [[Caspian tiger]].

One of two or more individuals sharing at least one [[Parent|parent]]. A male sibling is a [[Brother|brother]] and a female sibling is a [[Sister|sister]]; a person with no siblings is an only child. Most societies raise siblings together, which fosters strong emotional bonds, although the relationship is often complicated and influenced by parental treatment, birth order and personality. Medically, full siblings are first-degree relatives, related by 50%, and half-siblings are second-degree relatives, related by 25%. [[Twin|Twins]] are siblings born from the same pregnancy. Old English common law once gave half-siblings only half as much of their intestate siblings' estates as full siblings received. Such unequal treatment has been wholly abolished in England but still exists in Florida.

Inland province in southwestern [[China]], lying in the Sichuan Basin and the Tibetan Plateau. Its capital is [[Chengdu]], and its population is about 83 million. In antiquity the area was home to the kingdoms of Ba and Shu until their incorporation by the Qin around 316 BC. Devastated in the 17th century by Zhang Xianzhong's rebellion and the Manchu conquest, it recovered to become one of China's most productive areas by the 19th century. During World War II, [[Chongqing]] served as the temporary capital of the [[Republic of China (1912–1949)|Republic of China]]. Sichuan suffered gravely during the [[Great Chinese Famine]] (1959–1961) and remained China's most populous province until Chongqing was separated from it in 1997. The cuisine features the [[Sichuan pepper]], and the province is home to many [[Giant panda|giant panda]] breeding stations and reserves.

Chinese spice made from the dried pericarp (outer shell) of fruit from plants of the genus *Zanthoxylum*. Despite its name, it is not closely related to [[Black pepper|black pepper]] or [[Chili pepper|chili pepper]]; *Zanthoxylum* belongs to the same family as [[Citrus|citrus]] and rue. It produces a tingling, numbing effect due to hydroxy-alpha sanshool, and is used in Sichuan dishes such as mapo tofu, Kung Pao chicken and Chongqing hot pot. It is often added to chili peppers to create the flavor known as "málà" ("numb-spiciness").

Italian secret criminal society and criminal organization originating on the island of [[Sicily]]. Also called Cosa Nostra, it emerged in the mid-19th century as a form of local protection and control over land and agriculture. By the mid-20th century it had infiltrated politics, construction and finance, and expanded into [[Drug|drug]] trafficking and money laundering. Its basic group, the "family" or cosca, claims sovereignty over a territory, usually a town or neighborhood, where it operates its rackets. Emigration from Sicily led to mafia-style gangs in other countries, including the [[American Mafia]] in the United States.

Island in the central [[Mediterranean Sea]] forming an autonomous region of [[Italy]]. With over 4.7 million inhabitants, it is the largest and most populous island in the Mediterranean. Its most prominent landmark is [[Mount Etna]], the tallest active volcano in Europe, currently 3,403 m (11,165 ft) high. The earliest archaeological record of human activity dates to around 14,000 BC. By around 750 BC, Sicily had three Phoenician and around twelve Greek colonies along its coasts, and the [[Punic Wars]] of 264–146 BC were fought between Rome and [[Carthage]]. Ruled in the Early Middle Ages by the Vandals, Ostrogoths, Byzantine Empire and Emirate of Sicily, it became the County of Sicily after the Norman conquest in 1071, succeeded by the [[Kingdom of Sicily]] in 1130. After an invasion led by [[Giuseppe Garibaldi]] and a plebiscite, it joined unified Italy in 1860. It was granted autonomous status on 15 May 1946.

Single-handed agricultural tool with a variously curved blade, typically used to reap grain or cut forage for [[Livestock|livestock]]. Harvesting sickles, first developed around 15,000 years ago, had wooden handles and flint blades. Sickles helped drive the transition to [[Agriculture|agriculture]] in the Neolithic era, and their use is accepted as having led directly to the domestication of Near Eastern wild grasses. Hundreds of region-specific variants evolved from the start of the [[Iron Age]], first of iron and later of steel. The serrated blade that originated in prehistoric sickles still dominates grain reaping and appears in modern harvesting machines and some kitchen knives. The tool also played a prominent role in the [[Druid|Druids']] ritual of oak and mistletoe, as described by [[Pliny the Elder]].

Group of inherited blood disorders involving abnormal [[Hemoglobin|hemoglobin]]. Abnormal red blood cells adopt a sickle-like shape that cannot deform as they pass through capillaries, causing blockages. The disease occurs when a person inherits two abnormal copies of the β-globin gene, one from each parent. Attacks of pain, called sickle cell crises, can be triggered by temperature changes, stress, dehydration and high altitude. As of 2021, it was estimated to affect about 7.7 million people worldwide, and about 80% of cases occur in [[Sub-Saharan Africa]]. Carriers with a single abnormal gene have some protection against [[Malaria]].

Indian actor and model. He appeared mainly in [[Hindi]] television and films, rising to prominence in *Balika Vadhu*. He won the reality shows *Bigg Boss 13* and *Fear Factor: Khatron Ke Khiladi 7*, and hosted *Savdhaan India* and *India's Got Talent*. In 2005 he became the first Indian and the first Asian to win the World's Best Model title. He made his acting debut in 2008 in *Babul Ka Aangann Chootey Na*, and his Bollywood debut in 2014 in a supporting role in *Humpty Sharma Ki Dulhania*.

Canadian ice hockey center and captain of the [[Pittsburgh]] Penguins of the [[National Hockey League]]. Selected first overall by the Penguins in the 2005 NHL entry draft, he was among the most lauded prospects in hockey history. In his second season he led the league with 120 points, winning the Art Ross Trophy and the Hart Memorial Trophy as most valuable player. Crosby captained Pittsburgh to Stanley Cup championships in 2009, 2016 and 2017. He won Olympic gold with Canada in 2010, scoring the overtime winner in the final, and again in 2014 as captain.

Bahamian-American actor, filmmaker, diplomat and author. Born in [[Miami]] while his Bahamian parents were visiting, he was raised in the Bahamas before moving to New York City at age 16 to act. In 1964 he became the first Black male actor and first Bahamian to win the Academy Award for Best Actor, for *Lilies of the Field* (1963). His 1967 films addressing race and race relations included *To Sir, with Love*, *Guess Who's Coming to Dinner* and *In the Heat of the Night*. He made his directorial debut with *Buck and the Preacher* (1972). Queen [[Elizabeth II]] granted him an honorary knighthood in 1974. He served as Bahamian ambassador to Japan from 1997 to 2007, and in 2009 President [[Barack Obama]] awarded him the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

Military blockade of a city or fortress, intended to conquer it by attrition or by a well-prepared assault. Attackers surround the target to block supplies, reinforcement and escape, then reduce its fortifications with siege engines, artillery or mining. Sieges can be decided by starvation, thirst or [[Disease|disease]], which may take months or even years. Ancient cities in the Middle East had fortified walls, and the walls of the Sumerian city of [[Uruk]] were 9.5 km (5.9 mi) long and up to 12 m (39 ft) high. During the [[Renaissance]] and early modern period, siege warfare dominated the conduct of war in Europe, and [[Leonardo da Vinci]] gained renown from designing fortifications. Cannons in the Napoleonic era reduced the value of fortifications. Modern sieges more often result from hostage, militant or resisting-arrest situations.

Axis blockade of Leningrad (present-day [[Saint Petersburg]]) during [[World War II]]. Germany and Finland besieged the Soviet city for 872 days without capturing it. Land routes were cut on 8 September 1941, and Germany chose to starve the city rather than capture it. Many residents starved in the winter of 1941–1942. Supplies arrived by air, by ship across [[Lake Ladoga]] and over the Road of Life. A Red Army offensive opened a land corridor on 18 January 1943, and the siege was fully broken on 27 January 1944. An estimated 1.5 million died, making it possibly the deadliest siege in history.

Prolonged military [[Blockade|blockade]] of [[Sarajevo]], capital of [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]], during the [[Bosnian War]]. Lasting 1,425 days, from 5 April 1992 to 29 February 1996, it is regarded as the longest siege of a capital city in modern warfare. Bosnian Serb forces bombarded the city with artillery, tanks, mortars and sniper fire, firing an estimated 500,000 shells. 13,952 people were killed, including 5,434 civilians. After the second Markale massacre on 28 August 1995, [[NATO]] launched an air campaign, and the Dayton Peace Agreement was signed in December 1995. Bosnian Serb leaders Radovan Karadžić and Ratko Mladić were convicted of crimes against humanity.

Final major land engagement of the [[American Revolutionary War]], fought in 1781 at Yorktown, Virginia. The Continental Army under [[George Washington]] and French allies besieged a British army commanded by Charles Cornwallis. A French fleet under the Comte de Grasse defeated a British relief fleet at the Battle of the Chesapeake, blocking escape by sea. On October 14, a column led by [[Alexander Hamilton]] took a key British redoubt. Cornwallis surrendered on October 19, with more than 7,000 British soldiers captured. Negotiations followed, producing the [[Treaty of Paris (1783)|Treaty of Paris]] in 1783.

German multinational company focused on industrial automation, rail transport and health technology. Founded in 1847 as the Telegraphen-Bauanstalt von Siemens & Halske in [[Berlin]] by Werner von Siemens and Johann Georg Halske, it took its present form in 1966 through a merger of three companies. It is the largest engineering company in Europe and employs about 320,000 people, with headquarters in [[Munich]] and Berlin. It reported global revenue of around €78 billion in 2023. Siemens Healthineers (2017) and Siemens Energy (2020) were later spun off.

SI unit of electric conductance, the reciprocal of the [[Ohm|ohm]]. One siemens (symbol S) equals one [[Ampere|ampere]] per [[Volt|volt]], so a device with a conductance of one siemens passes one ampere more for every volt of potential difference across it. The unit is also used for electric susceptance and admittance, and conductivity is measured in siemens per meter (S/m). The siemens was adopted by the International Electrotechnical Commission in 1935 and added as an SI derived unit at the 14th General Conference on Weights and Measures in 1971. It is named after Ernst Werner von Siemens. The older name mho, the ohm spelled backwards, is an unaccepted special name that NIST says should be strictly avoided.

[[Fractal]] with the overall shape of an equilateral triangle, subdivided recursively into smaller equilateral triangles. Named after the Polish mathematician Wacław Sierpiński, it is one of the basic examples of self-similar sets, a mathematically generated pattern that repeats at any magnification or reduction. It can be constructed by repeatedly removing the central triangle from each subdivided triangle. The pattern appeared as a decorative motif many centuries before Sierpiński's work.

Country on the west coast of [[West Africa]], with its capital at [[Freetown]]. It is bordered by [[Liberia]] to the southeast and [[Guinea]] to the north. Its land area is 73,252 km² (28,283 sq mi), and the 2023 census counted 8,460,512 people. Sierra Leone is a presidential republic, and Muslims constitute three-quarters of the population, with a significant Christian minority. The coastal Sierra Leone Colony was founded in 1808 as part of the [[British Empire]], as a place to resettle Africans returning after the abolition of the slave trade. Independence from the [[United Kingdom]] came in 1961. A civil war that began in 1991 between the government and the Revolutionary United Front ended with the rebels' defeat in 2002. The country is rich in diamonds, gold, [[Bauxite|bauxite]] and aluminum, but in the 2019 survey 59.2% of the population was affected by multidimensional poverty.

Mountain range in the [[Western United States]], between the Central Valley of [[California]] and the Great Basin. Most of the range lies in California, though its Carson Range spur lies primarily in [[Nevada]]. It runs 400 mi (640 km) north–south and is 50 to 80 mi (80 to 130 km) wide. [[Lake Tahoe]] is the largest alpine lake in North America, and Mount Whitney, at 14,505 ft (4,421 m), is the highest point in the contiguous United States. Yosemite Valley was sculpted by glaciers from granite more than 100 million years old. The range started to uplift less than five million years ago, and erosion exposed the light-colored granite that forms its mountains and cliffs. The California gold rush occurred in its western foothills from 1848 through 1855. Its three national parks include Yosemite, Sequoia and Kings Canyon.
